topic: Disability tax credit approval as the gateway: Child Disability Benefit, RDSP grants/bond, Canada Disability Benefit all require DTC eligibility

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): Noah, 10, Manitoba, DTC-eligible, no income so no tax on his own return (the unused credit may be transferable to a supporting person; not covered here). Amounts are maximums for the benefit year July 2026 – June 2027 (CDB child, Canada Disability Benefit) and per year (RDSP); all are income-tested except the matching grant's basic rate.

spoken.child_dis: three thousand four hundred and eighty dollars
spoken.cdb_month: two hundred and four dollars and twenty cents

sources.child_dis: canada.ca Child disability benefit: up to $3,480/yr ($290/month) per child eligible for the DTC, July 2026–June 2027, reduced when AFNI > $82,847; paid with the CCB (search 2026-10-24)
sources.rdsp: canada.ca (ESDC) How much you could get in grants and bonds: grant up to $3,500/yr, $70,000 lifetime (matching contributions, until the end of the year the beneficiary turns 49); bond up to $1,000/yr, $20,000 lifetime, no contribution needed, low income; beneficiary must be DTC-eligible (search 2026-10-24)
sources.cdb: canada.ca Canada Disability Benefit – How much you could receive: up to $204.20/month July 2026–June 2027, income-tested on 2025 AFNI; eligibility: DTC-eligible, age 18–64, resident, filed prior-year return (search 2026-10-24)
sources.dtc: ITA 118.3(1): severe and prolonged impairment, marked restriction certified by a medical practitioner in prescribed form (T2201); non-refundable credit reduces tax payable
sources.overlap: LF-05 (long-form DTC) covers who qualifies / who signs / up to 10 years back; this Short avoids those angles
